purpose: Compare Cue's Qloo-grounded recommendation slate against an independent LLM-only baseline on identical briefs, with preregistered metrics, thresholds, and hypothesis outcomes.
note: This file was committed before the comparative metrics were computed. Its sha256 is recorded in benchmark/results.json so a reader can confirm the metrics were not redefined after seeing results.

A.label: LLM-only baseline
A.description: The ungrounded answer produced by the model alone, with no Qloo data. Sourced from CueSheet.baseline, which the production pipeline already builds as its own control group.
A.measuredOutputSize: whatever the model returned; recorded, never padded

B.label: Cue (Qloo-powered)
B.description: The production pipeline: Qloo resolves anchors and tags, ranks artists by measured affinity, and assembles the slate.
inputWhitelist: the same scene string as Arm A
B.declaredOutputSize: up to the pool size; recorded

slateSizeParity.rule: Arm A returns exactly 3 cues by construction. All size-sensitive metrics are therefore computed at k = 3, truncating Arm B to its top 3 by measured affinity. Full-length Arm B figures are also reported but are explicitly labelled not size-matched.
slateSizeParity.justification: Comparing a 3-item answer against a 6-8 item answer would confound slate size with every size-sensitive metric. k = 3 is the largest size both arms can supply, and it requires no change to production code because truncation happens in this harness.
slateSizeParity.affinityTiebreak: affinity descending, then popularity descending, then entity_id ascending (deterministic)

poolParity.statement: Arm A is never given a candidate pool; it answers open-book from parametric knowledge. Arm B selects from the pool Qloo returned for the brief. Pool parity is therefore NOT achievable without changing the production prompt.
poolParity.mitigation: Both arms are scored against the SAME pool for the coverage metric. Arm A picks that do not appear in the pool are recorded as unmeasurable, never imputed as zero.
poolParity.smallestSafeChangeProposed: Add a benchmark-only closed-book variant that supplies the identical candidate list to the model, so both arms choose from one pool. This requires a new prompt and is deliberately NOT implemented here, because it would change what Arm A means and is a production-adjacent change beyond this task's scope.

anchorTreatment.definition: An anchor is a named artist explicitly present in the brief's scene text and in the brief's resolved anchors[] field. Matching is case-insensitive after stripping punctuation, and matches on whole tokens only.
anchorTreatment.source: Both arms share the identical brief object from the same response, so the anchor set is identical across arms by construction.
anchorTreatment.metric: anchorRecycling = |{items naming an anchor}| / |items|, at the common slate size.

briefs.scene: A late-night drive home through a rainy city. Melancholy and cinematic, late 90s trip hop. The character is alone with their thoughts after a funeral.
briefs.inclusionReason: Baseline domain; era 1990s; melancholy mood; no named anchors.

briefs.scene: A modern noir procedural cold open. Tense and brooding, a sparse electronic score under a city at night. The detective finds the file they were not supposed to see. 2020s.
briefs.inclusionReason: Era 2020s; tension mood; electronic genre; no named anchors; different domain from brief 1.

briefs.scene: A 1970s family drama. Warm and nostalgic, grounded in soul and funk. A Curtis Mayfield record plays on the kitchen radio while the family argues about money.
briefs.inclusionReason: Era 1970s; nostalgia mood; soul genre; names an anchor, so anchor recycling is measurable.

briefs.scene: A contemporary sports montage. Euphoric and triumphant, high-energy afrobeats and hip hop. The underdog team trains at dawn before the final. 2020s.
briefs.inclusionReason: Era 2020s; euphoria mood; afrobeats genre; non-Western genre emphasis; no named anchors.

briefs.scene: A Nordic noir scene. Ominous and intimate, minimal classical piano and ambient texture. Snow, silence, a long corridor. In the spirit of Nils Frahm.
briefs.inclusionReason: Era 2010s; ominous mood; classical genre; names an anchor.

briefs.scene: An 1980s teen comedy. Hopeful and euphoric, synthwave and pop. The protagonist rides a bike at sunset after finally fitting in. 1980s.
briefs.inclusionReason: Era 1980s; hope mood; synthwave genre; no named anchors; completes the era spread.

briefInclusionCriteria: The scene string is at least one full sentence and at least 20 characters, so the production route accepts it.
The set spans at least four distinct decades and at least five distinct moods.
At least two briefs name an explicit anchor, so anchor recycling is measurable.
At least two briefs name no anchor, so anchor recycling is not trivially zero for both arms.
No brief was selected on the basis of how well either arm performed on it. Briefs were fixed before any comparative result was computed.

M1_briefRelevance.label: Brief relevance (lexical facet-match proxy)
M1_briefRelevance.warning: This is a word-overlap proxy, NOT a human judgement of relevance and NOT a measure of quality. It rewards restating the brief's vocabulary and is reported per facet so a reader can audit it.
M1_briefRelevance.formula: For each item, a facet is matched when any of the facet's tokens appears in the item's searchable text (artist + track + rationale, lowercased, punctuation stripped). itemRelevance = matchedFacets / 4. slateRelevance = mean(itemRelevance).
M1_briefRelevance.range: 0..1, higher means more brief vocabulary echoed
M1_briefRelevance.tieHandling: Exact rational counts; no ties possible at the item level.

M2_anchorRecycling.label: Anchor recycling
M2_anchorRecycling.warning: Measures repetition of names already in the brief. High is worse. It is not a quality measure on its own: naming a requested anchor can be correct.
M2_anchorRecycling.formula: anchorRecycling = |{items whose artist or track names an anchor}| / |items|

M3_diversity.label: Recommendation diversity
M3_diversity.warning: distinctArtistRatio is structural. textJaccard is a lexical proxy for content variety and is labelled as such. tagRedundancy is Arm B only because Arm A has no tags.

formula.textJaccard: mean over unordered item pairs of |tokens(a) intersect tokens(b)| / |tokens(a) union tokens(b)|, tokens from artist + track + rationale
formula.tagRedundancy: reused from Cue's production coverage result (Arm B only)

M3_diversity.crossArmComparable: distinctArtistRatio and textJaccard: yes. tagRedundancy: Arm B only.

M4_tagCoverage.label: Tag Coverage Index
M4_tagCoverage.warning: Reused from src/lib/coverage.ts with NO formula change. Pool-relative: it is not a share of listeners and is NOT a measure of recommendation quality.
M4_tagCoverage.tieHandling: Not applicable; deterministic given a pool and a slate.
M4_tagCoverage.crossArmComparable: Conditionally. Arm A items that do not resolve into the pool are recorded as unmeasurable, never scored as zero.
M4_tagCoverage.unmeasurableRule: If fewer than the common slate size of Arm A items resolve into the pool, coverage is reported as unavailable with a reason, and excluded from aggregate comparison.

M5_humanPreference.label: Human preference (blinded review)
M5_humanPreference.warning: Only genuine blinded reviews may populate this. No automated score is ever substituted for it. It is not computed unless real reviewers submit reviews.
M5_humanPreference.formula: Mean of submitted 1-5 ratings per criterion, per arm, after unblinding. Criteria: relevance, variety, would-use.
M5_humanPreference.blinding: Arm labels are replaced by per-brief labels derived deterministically from the protocol hash, so reviewers cannot tell which is which and the mapping is reproducible.
M5_humanPreference.availabilityRule: If no review files are present, results must record available=false with a reason. Never synthesise ratings.

aggregation.primaryRule: Per-metric per-brief differences (B minus A) at the common slate size.
aggregation.signTest: Count briefs agreeing with the predicted direction.
aggregation.supportedStrong: 6 of 6 briefs agree AND median difference is at least the meaningful threshold.
aggregation.supportedWeak: 5 of 6 briefs agree AND median difference is at least the meaningful threshold.
aggregation.powerDisclosure: With n = 6 briefs, a one-sided sign test reaches p = 0.0156 at 6/6 and p = 0.109 at 5/6. A 5/6 result therefore CANNOT be called significant at alpha = 0.05 and is labelled weak. This is stated in advance so a weak result is not later presented as strong.
aggregation.noCompositeScore: The five metrics are deliberately NOT combined into one score. No defensible weighting scheme exists without human preference data, so no composite is reported.

M1_briefRelevance.justification: One facet out of four is 0.25 at item level; 0.10 is a little under half a facet of mean movement, the smallest shift that would change how a reader describes the answer.

M2_anchorRecycling.justification: One extra recycled item is 0.33 of a 3-item slate. 0.20 is above half an item, so it cannot be produced by a single tie-break flip.

M3_diversity.justification: One extra distinct artist in a 3-item slate is 0.33; in a 6-item slate, 0.17. 0.15 is the smallest change that survives at the larger slate size.

M4_tagCoverage.justification: The repository's own revision gains are 8.1, 21.6 and 3.2 index points, so 10 points is above the smallest gain the project already treats as material, and below the largest.

H1_diversity.claim: Arm B has a higher distinctArtistRatio than Arm A.
H1_diversity.note: Arm A is prompted for 3 artists and often returns distinct names, so this may not hold.

H2_anchorRecycling.claim: Arm B recycles brief anchors less than Arm A.
H2_anchorRecycling.note: Arm A is prompted from the brief text, so it is expected to name the famous anchor.

H3_coverage.claim: Arm B's slate reaches a higher Tag Coverage Index than Arm A's picks where Arm A's picks are measurable in the pool.
H3_coverage.preregisteredCaveat: This is expected to be INCONCLUSIVE BY CONSTRUCTION. Arm A answers open-book, so many of its picks will not exist in Arm B's pool, and coverage will be unmeasurable for those. A low Arm A coverage figure is therefore evidence about the measurement's applicability, not evidence that Arm B recommends better music.
H3_coverage.note: If Arm A picks are unmeasurable, the outcome must be recorded as inconclusive, not as a win for Arm B.

H4_briefRelevance.claim: Arm A matches brief vocabulary at least as well as Arm B.
H4_briefRelevance.note: Stated against the project's interest on purpose: a fluent model is expected to echo the brief's own words well. This hypothesis exists so that an unfavourable result is predicted rather than explained away.

evidenceThatWouldSupport: 6 of 6 briefs agreeing in the predicted direction with median difference at or above the meaningful threshold, on live executions where both arms ran with their declared provenance.
evidenceThatWouldContradict: 5 or more of 6 briefs agreeing in the opposite direction, or a median difference in the opposite direction above the threshold.
evidenceThatWouldLeaveInconclusive: Fewer than 5 of 6 briefs agreeing, a median difference below the threshold, any brief where either arm degraded to sample output, or any metric that is unmeasurable for either arm.

failureHandling.armA_degraded: If baseline.source is not 'llm', the arm degraded to a fixed sample. The brief is recorded as excluded with that reason and is NOT scored.
failureHandling.armB_degraded: If the response mode is not 'live', the brief is recorded as excluded with that reason and is NOT scored.
failureHandling.qlooRequestFailures: Recorded per brief from receipts with status != 200. A non-zero count is reported, never hidden.
failureHandling.missingMetric: Recorded as null with a reason string. Never coerced to zero.
failureHandling.networkFailure: The recording step aborts without overwriting existing evidence. Replay never needs the network.

provenanceRequirements: sha256 of each raw evidence file
model source, model id and provider reported by the deployment
HTTP status and latency per brief
a per-brief label separating live execution, recorded replay, and sample output

determinism.replay: npm run benchmark recomputes every metric from committed raw evidence and the frozen protocol, then asserts the recomputed results equal the committed results artifact.
